title: Beavers were last recorded around Loch Ness in about 1527; nearly 500 years later, Scotland has licensed conservation groups to release up to 15 beaver families into the River Ness catchment over three years.
summary_full: Scotland has approved a three-year project to reintroduce beavers to the River Ness catchment. Conservation organizations will relocate beaver families from other parts of Scotland to promote healthy populations. Beavers are recognized as ecosystem engineers that contribute to the restoration of natural habitats. Their return aims to improve ecological balance and support diverse wildlife in the region.
